issues.legal_issue: Land inherited or received by bequest by a female after the commencement of a land-ceiling law does not qualify for the special allowance for stridhana land when the statutory definition limits that category to land held by her at commencement.
material_facts: The land was bequeathed to the landholder and his wife under a will, and the wife acquired title only after the land-ceiling law had commenced, when the testatrix died.
The wife did not hold the land on the law’s commencement date.
The land tribunal allowed the wife to retain the bequeathed land as stridhana land, but the High Court set that decision aside in a revision concerning determination of surplus agricultural land.
issues.conclusion: The wife’s post-commencement acquisition was not stridhana land eligible for the special allowance, and the High Court was right that the allowance did not apply. The land was liable to be included in the family’s holding when surplus land was determined.
issues.legal_principle: The definition of “stridhana land” in section 3(42) is restricted to land held in a female family member’s own name on the commencement date, and section 5(4)(a) grants its allowance only for land within that definition. Section 21 does not distinguish post-commencement acquisitions by inheritance or bequest that are described as stridhana from other property for this purpose. This reading accords with the law’s purpose of acquiring surplus agricultural land for distribution and with the definition’s express temporal limit; the term is not used in its Hindu-law sense. The contrary decision in Valliammal v. The Authorised Officer, Land Reforms, Coimbatore, A.I.R. 1973 Mad 321, was overruled.

predicates.land_ceiling_surplus_determination: An authority was determining surplus agricultural land under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.land_acquired_by_female_after_commenceme: A female family member acquired the land by inheritance or bequest after the ceiling scheme commenced.
predicates.female_did_not_hold_land_at_commencement: The female family member did not hold that land when the ceiling scheme commenced.

issues.definition: When surplus land is being determined, land acquired by a female family member after commencement, where she did not hold it at commencement, is not eligible for the special allowance.

issues.legal_issue: A claim based on amendments made after the decision under appeal need not be examined afresh in that appeal when the claimant may pursue appropriate proceedings under the amended law.
material_facts: During the appeal, the appellant relied on amendments made to the land-ceiling law after the relevant orders.
The Court declined to examine the case afresh under those amendments and left the appellant free to seek any available benefit through appropriate proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Court would not reconsider the case under the subsequent amendments in this appeal; the appellant could pursue appropriate proceedings to claim any benefit available under the amended law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it inadvisable to examine the appeal afresh under subsequent amendments and expressly left the parties free to take appropriate action under those amendments. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was relied on for this procedural disposition.

predicates.appeal_pending: A party’s challenge to an earlier decision was pending before an appellate court.
predicates.subsequent_amendments_invoked: A party asked the appellate court to reconsider the matter in light of amendments made after the decision under challenge.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending and subsequent amendments are invoked, the claim under those amendments may be left for appropriate proceedings rather than examined afresh in that appeal.
